subject: Limits on Damages — annual-reset vs. aggregate exposure (MSA redlines)
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Harrison & Lee <contracts@harrisonlee.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial MSA redlines attached — liability cap questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the good conversation last week. We've attached Acme's redlines to the MSA for your review (ACME-MSA-redlines-v2.docx). Our legal team has flagged the limitation of liability section for a commercial discussion — specifically: whether the cap should be annualized (reset each 12-month period), measured as a multiple of fees paid, or aggregate over the full term.

Acme's initial posture is: aggregate cap equal to the greater of $3M or 2x fees paid during the prior 12 months. Our procurement lead would prefer an annual reset to avoid a large lump-sum exposure for multi-year contracts. We included comments in the doc about carve-outs for IP indemnity, breach-of-confidentiality, and willful misconduct.

Could Redwood propose one commercial approach and one fallback to move contracting forward quickly? Also: Acme needs a specific sublimit or carveout for data incidents (we've suggested $5M or 3x fees, whichever is greater) — happy to discuss.

Attached: ACME-MSA-redlines-v2.docx

Regards,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Procurement, Acme Analytics
olivia.barnes@acme.com

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-15T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines attached — liability cap questions

Olivia — thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. I reviewed the doc and have two practical proposals from a commercial perspective:

Option A (preferred for risk alignment):
- Aggregate liability cap equal to the greater of $4M or 3x fees paid in the preceding 12 months (no per-year reset).
- Carveouts: IP indemnity, breach of confidentiality, fraud/willful misconduct.
- Consequential and punitive damages excluded except where required by law and for breach of confidentiality/IP.

Option B (close-and-move approach):
- Annual-reset cap: liability limited each contract year to the greater of $1M or 1x fees paid in that year (resets annually).
- Same carveouts as above. Aggregate exposure therefore could exceed the aggregate if multiple years.

Commercial rationale: Option A gives Acme and Redwood clearer single-number exposure for procurement and exec reporting; Option B tends to be more acceptable for buyers concerned about a single large aggregate cap for multi-year deals. If Acme needs a specific sublimit for data incidents, Redwood can accept a $5M sublimit subject to acceptable indemnity wording and notice/mitigation obligations.

I'm attaching our counter redlines (Redwood-counter-MSA-redlines-20280715.docx) that implement Option B as a compromise (annual-reset) because that is most likely to speed procurement. Laura — can you please run legal-level redlines on our doc (esp. the IP carveouts and the precise exclusion language for consequential damages)?

Next step: Laura/Legal to propose firm language and Karthik/Commercial to indicate which option we can present as our standard fallback. If Acme pushes aggregate, we'll need a brief exec approval for higher aggregate exposures.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood-counter-MSA-redlines-20280715.docx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme.com>
Date: 2028-07-16T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MSA redlines attached — liability cap questions

Marissa / Karthik — I reviewed the counter and Acme's markups. High-level legal position and suggested wording:

1) Cap mechanics: we should prefer an annual-reset cap in commercial documents when the customer requests it (helps close). However, we should insist on an overall aggregate floor for catastrophic events handled via insurance/exec approval. Suggested language: "Aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) $1,000,000 per 12-month period, or (ii) the total fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim; provided, however, that Redwood's liability for claims arising from a breach of the Data Processing Addendum, willful misconduct, or Redwood's indemnity obligations for third-party IP infringement shall not be subject to the foregoing limitation to the extent such limitation would prevent the recovery of direct damages as required by applicable law."

2) Carveouts: must explicitly include IP indemnity and data breach costs (investigation/notification/remediation/legal fees) — we can propose a sublimit for PII incidents of $5,000,000 or 3x fees paid, whichever is greater. This preserves commercial flexibility but signals seriousness on security incidents.

3) Consequential damages: keep a broad exclusion, but carve back for breach of confidentiality/DPAs and IP indemnity. Avoid vague "special" damage categories.

4) Insurance and notice: require customer to provide notice within 30 days of discovery and require Redwood to be given reasonable mitigation control. Also confirm that both parties maintain cyber insurance with minimum limits (we can negotiate amounts offline).

I'll prepare a tracked-redline draft with the suggested text (will attach PDF of notes). Karthik: if we plan to present Option B (annual reset) as the counter, confirm that Sales is comfortable with the $1M floor and the proposed PII sublimit — if not, we can present Option A to avoid exec approvals.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Limits on Damages — annual-reset vs. aggregate exposure (MSA redlines)

Quick commercial note: prefer Option B (annual-reset) to keep the deal velocity. Procurement at Acme has told me they'd accept an annual reset as long as the per-year floor is not below $1M and there's a clear PII sublimit. If legal is comfortable with the carveouts and the notice/insurance asks, I'm happy to present the counter this week.

If Acme insists on aggregate 3x fees, that'll need an exec sign-off and possibly a pricing concession. Recommend we aim to close with annual-reset + $5M PII sublimit.

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Limits on Damages — annual-reset vs. aggregate exposure (MSA redlines)

Olivia — thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's near-final counter implementing the annual-reset approach (Redwood-counter-MSA-redlines-20280715.docx) with the following commercial compromise:

- Liability cap per 12-month period: the greater of $1,000,000 or the fees paid in the preceding 12 months (resets each year).
- Specific carveouts: IP indemnity and breach-of-confidentiality (not subject to the liability cap).
- PII/data incident sublimit: $5,000,000 or 3x fees paid during the prior 12 months, whichever is greater, subject to agreed notice and mitigation procedures.
- Consequential damages excluded except for breach of confidentiality and IP indemnity.
- Requirement for both parties to maintain cyber insurance; Redwood will provide certificate upon request.

Laura — please confirm final legal language and whether the PII sublimit triggers any additional indemnity flow or premium insurance requirements. Stephanie — can you confirm whether this approach needs an exec exception to present as our standard counter? My ask: if legal signs off on the wording, I'd like to present this as our standard next-version counter to Acme tomorrow and request procurement to route the DocuSign.

Olivia — if Acme is aligned on these commercial numbers, we can push DocuSign and get the order form processed next week.

Attachments: Redwood-counter-MSA-redlines-20280715.docx, OrderForm-ACME-2028.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
